The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2)^{′}=-\frac{1}{x}+1
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-2}{(-\frac{1}{{x}_{n}}+1)} \\  & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}({x}_{n}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-2)}{{x}_{n}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}({x}_{n}-1)-{x}_{n}({x}_{n}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-2)}{{x}_{n}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}+1)}{{x}_{n}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{{x}_{0}(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{0}+1)}{{x}_{0}-1} \\  & =\frac{0.1\,(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.1)+1)}{0.1-1} \\  & =0.144…\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{{x}_{1}(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{1}+1)}{{x}_{1}-1} \\  & =\frac{0.144…(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.144…)+1)}{0.144⋯-1} \\  & =0.157…, \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{{x}_{2}(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{2}+1)}{{x}_{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{0.157…(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.157…)+1)}{0.157⋯-1} \\  & =0.158….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈0.16$ and ${x}_{3}≈0.16$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x≈0.16,$ rounded to two decimal places.
html:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

xn+1=xn−f(xn)f′(xn)

where f′(xn) is the derivative of f(x) evaluated at xn.

In our case, we have

f′(x)=(x−ln⁡x−2)′=−1x+1

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−xn−ln⁡xn−2(−1xn+1)=xn−xn(xn−ln⁡xn−2)xn−1=xn(xn−1)−xn(xn−ln⁡xn−2)xn−1=xn(ln⁡xn+1)xn−1.

Starting with x0=0.1, we have

x1=x0(ln⁡x0+1)x0−1=0.1(ln⁡(0.1)+1)0.1−1=0.144…

Similarly, we have

x2=x1(ln⁡x1+1)x1−1=0.144…(ln⁡(0.144…)+1)0.144⋯−1=0.157…,x3=x2(ln⁡x2+1)x2−1=0.157…(ln⁡(0.157…)+1)0.157⋯−1=0.158….

Notice that the last two approximations x2≈0.16 and x3≈0.16 are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is x≈0.16, rounded to two decimal places.
